verses.1: And when the Pharisees and Sadducees came forward, they asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
verses.2: And the one who answered said to them, “You say that it has become bright. But Eudia, indeed, the sky is burning.”
verses.3: And now it’s winter. The sky is becoming dark and cold. You can’t distinguish the features of the sky at all; you also can’t tell the signs of the seasons.
verses.4: It’s a wicked and deceitful sign that is desired. But such a sign won’t be given to her, unless the sign of Zion is given as well. And so, they were left behind.
verses.5: And when the disciples went outside, they went to get some food.
verses.6: But Jesus said to them, “Watch out for the schemes of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
verses.7: But those who were in disagreement with each other said that they would not take Artus along.
verses.8: But Jesus said, “Why do you argue with yourselves, foolish people? Why don’t you take some food?”
verses.9: And don’t you remember either the five kinds of bread that were part of those fifty thousand pieces of bread, and how many heads of cattle you took away from them.
verses.10: And how many of those seven kinds of fruits did you take, and how many seeds did you collect?
verses.11: Don’t you realize that we said “not about food”? Be careful with the tricks of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
verses.12: Then it became clear that he didn’t mean to say that one should avoid the toxins in food, but rather that one should avoid the teachings of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
verses.13: When Jesus came to the regions of Galilee, he asked his disciples, “What do people say about the Son of Man?”
verses.14: And they said: Some said that it was John the Baptist; others said Elyas; still others said Jeremiah or one of the prophets.
verses.15: He says to them: “What do you call me?”
verses.16: Then Simon Peter replied, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
verses.17: Then Jesus replied to him, “Happy you, Simon Barjona! It’s good that your flesh and blood weren’t revealed to you, but rather my Father in heaven.”
verses.18: I tell you therefore that you are Peter. And on this rock I will build my church. No gates of darkness will be able to separate it from it.
verses.19: I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven. If you lock them on earth, they will remain locked in heaven. And if you unlock them on earth, they will remain unlocked in heaven.
verses.20: Then he commanded his disciples that no one should say that he was the Christ.
verses.21: From that time on, Jesus began to show his disciples that he needed to go to Jerusalem. He had to endure many hardships at the hands of the elders, high priests, and officials. On the third day, he would rise from the dead.
verses.22: And when Peter hired him, he began to praise him, saying, “Well, my friend, this won’t be of any use to you.”
verses.23: But the traitor said to Peter, “Come back to me, Satan! I will destroy you, for you do not care about what God wants, but only about what people want.”
verses.24: Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone wants to come back to me, he must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.”
verses.25: For whoever wants to save his soul will surely be able to do so. But whoever tries to save his soul through me will surely fail.
verses.26: How can a person be satisfied if he gains the entire world but his soul is damaged in the process? Or what reward can a person give in exchange for his soul?
verses.27: For the son of man will come in the glory of his father at that time, along with his angels. And then he will reward each person according to their actions.
verses.28: I say to you that there are some among those who hold this position who will not experience death until they see the son of man coming into their kingdom.
